card.name: Subject nouns before a future prediction
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject noun phrase in news or science prose, just before a verb about what will happen or is likely to happen. Examples are 'that', 'Earth', 'people', 'yields' and 'work'.

modes.label: Subject before future verb
modes.description: A subject noun or pronoun right before a predicted future change.
modes.example: But<< that>> is about to change.

modes.label: Subject before hedged verb
modes.description: A subject noun right before 'may', 'are likely to' or similar hedging.
modes.example: another 100 million<< people>> may be forced into poverty by rising food

modes.label: Subject of a general claim
modes.description: A noun ending a subject phrase in a report on findings or trends.
modes.example: The World Bank has warned that world<< poverty>> is much greater than previously thought.

card.writes: It promotes hedging verbs such as 'may', 'might' and 'could', in English, Chinese and Spanish.
card.plain: It marks the end of a subject in news text where a hedged or predicted outcome is about to be stated.
